title: Spectral Localization Principle for Entanglement Harvesting
abstract: We propose a unified physical principle for entanglement harvesting: the entanglement that two localized detectors can extract from a quantum field is determined solely by how localized the field's effective spectral density is. We demonstrate this in an analytically solvable model of two qubits coupled to a leaky single-mode cavity, which in turn couples to a continuous electromagnetic bath, and derive the maximum harvestable concurrence in closed form, $\mathcal{C}_{\max}(Q)=2e^{-π/(2Q)}(1+e^{-π/(2Q)})/(1+3e^{-π/Q})$, where $Q\equiv|Δ|/κ$ is the ratio of the qubit-cavity detuning $Δ$ to the cavity linewidth $κ$. In the high-$Q$ limit, $\mathcal{C}_{\max}\simeq1-π^{2}/(16Q^{2})$, so the entanglement is robust against cavity loss; in the low-$Q$ limit it decays exponentially to zero, consistent with the irreversible-reservoir character of a continuous field, where maximal entanglement is unattainable. Since $Q$ is proportional to the inverse participation ratio (IPR) of the effective spectral density, it is the single dimensionless parameter governing the crossover from deterministic gate-based entanglement ($Q\to\infty$) to vacuum harvesting ($Q\to0$). Our framework operationalizes the Reeh-Schlieder theorem by quantifying the fraction of vacuum correlations accessible to localized detectors. It also reveals a formal correspondence of the maximal concurrence with the IPR, analogous to the conductivity-participation-ratio relation in Anderson localization. The predicted $\mathcal{C}_{\max}(Q)$ curve is, in principle, directly observable in superconducting circuit QED experiments.
summary: This work proposes the Spectral Localization Principle, stating that extractable entanglement depends only on how localized the field's spectral density is. Using an analytically solvable model of qubits coupled to a leaky cavity, the authors derive a closed-form expression for maximum concurrence based on the parameter $Q$. This framework bridges deterministic gate operations with vacuum harvesting by drawing formal analogies to localization phenomena.
main_problem: To establish a unified physical principle—the Spectral Localization Principle—governing how much entanglement can be extracted from a quantum field by localized detectors.
main_result: The maximum harvestable concurrence, $C_{\max}(Q)$, is determined solely by the spectral localization parameter $Q$, showing robustness in the high-$Q$ limit and exponential decay in the low-$Q$ limit.
method: Analytical derivation of the maximum concurrence using an analytically solvable model and applying adiabatic elimination to derive an effective master equation for the qubits.
model_or_system: The system consists of two qubits coupled to a leaky single-mode cavity, which is itself coupled to a continuous electromagnetic bath. The dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation after eliminating the cavity degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Maximum harvestable concurrence ($\mathcal{C}_{\max}$), which quantifies accessible vacuum correlations.
important_parameters: $Q \equiv |\Delta|/\kappa$, the ratio of qubit-cavity detuning to cavity linewidth; $\kappa$ (linewidth); IPR (Inverse Participation Ratio).
main_assumptions: The model assumes a Born-Markov approximation and uses adiabatic elimination, which requires a large separation between qubit and cavity timescales.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the principle, models the system using coupled qubits/cavity/bath Hamiltonian, derives the master equation via adiabatic elimination, calculates $C_{\max}(Q)$ in closed form, and analyzes its behavior in high-Q (deterministic) and low-Q (vacuum harvesting) limits.
why_interesting: It directly connects concepts from condensed matter physics (Anderson localization, IPR) to quantum information theory (entanglement harvesting), providing a quantitative diagnostic tool for vacuum correlations observable in superconducting circuit QED experiments.
